title: Minimum String Length After Balanced Removals
summary: Given a string s made up of 'a' and 'b', repeatedly remove any substring where the count of 'a' equals the count of 'b'.
statement: Given a string s made up of 'a' and 'b', repeatedly remove any substring where the count of 'a' equals the count of 'b'. Concatenate the remaining parts. Return the minimum possible length of the string after any number of such operations.
constraints: s contains only a and b.
Repeatedly remove any substring containing equal counts of a and b.
Return the minimum possible remaining length.
hints: Removing a balanced substring preserves the global difference count(a)-count(b).
Therefore at least the absolute difference must remain.
Repeatedly pair one a with one b through balanced removals until only the majority character remains.
The invariant lower bound is attainable, so its absolute value is the minimum length.
editorial: The invariant lower bound is attainable, so its absolute value is the minimum length.

tests.explanation: The entire string has three of each character and can be removed.
Two a-b pairs can be removed, leaving one a.
